pending_commit.commit_message: nebraska: Remove 'name' from json file The name is the payload file's name. However, if the payload file changes after the paygen, then one should modify its json file too to reflect that. But that coupling is not necessary, because we can easily assume that for a payload with name 'foo-payload.bin', its json file is 'foo-payload.bin.json'. Hence, the payload name can be drived from the json file itself and no need to modify the content of the json file. Just rename both files accordingly. nebraska: Handle critical updates We need to be able to handle critical updates for testing this feature in autotests. Critical updates (or blocking updates) are defined when the response to the client contains the attribute deadline="now" in one of the actions tag along with other parameters passed to the client. Users of Nebraska as a library can pass the critical_update argument to GetResponsetorequest() for this feature. tast: Introduce chromeos-base/tast-build-deps. This CL introduces the chromeos-base/tast-build-deps package where build time dependencies of all Tast related binaries (test runners and test bundles) are put. This package resolves a few problems about interaction between Portage and Tast: - Portage has a bug that --onlydeps-with-rdeps=n is ignored in a certain situation (https://bugs.gentoo.org/682472) and Tast had to work around the bug in a hacky and incomplete way when installing build time dependencies. The hack is no longer required after introduction of this package since the new package has no runtime-only dependency. - Formerly users were prompted to emerge dependencies even just after running update_chroot because local test dependencies were not installed to the host, adding tens of seconds to the runtime of the tast command. Now those dependencies are installed by update_chroot, so there is no need of additional emerge. FROMGIT: mmc: sdhci: sdhci-pci-o2micro: Correctly set bus width when tuning The O2Micro controller only supports tuning at 4-bits. So the host driver needs to change the bus width while tuning and then set it back when done. There was a bug in the original implementation in that mmc->ios.bus_width also wasn't updated. Thus setting the incorrect blocksize in sdhci_send_tuning which results in a tuning failure. tast: Remove -checktestdeps=auto flag value. -checktestdeps controls the behavior to skip tests by checking software dependencies. Formerly the flag had three values: always, never, auto. The auto value, which was actually the default when the flag is not explicitly specified, indicates that software deps should be checked if and only if tests are specified by attribute expressions (e.g. "(!disabled)") rather than exact names (e.g. "arc.Boot") or globs (e.g. "arc.*"). Since this behavior is confusing, this CL changes the flag to accept a boolean value, and sets the default to always checking software dependencies. Fortunately, there is no use of the flag in production today: http://cs/search/?q=%22-checktestdeps%22 BUG=chromium:971486 TEST=fast_build.sh -T TEST=fast_build.sh && ~/go/bin/tast run betty arc.Boot audio.DevicePlay Change-Id: I3edb2eaca0ccd84f5826eb75362000d482906c27 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1666817 Tested-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hidehiko Abe <hidehiko@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Keigo Oka <oka@chromium.org>

wifi_proxy: update scanning defaults These changed a long time ago (https://crrev.com/c/1126928) and a *very* long time ago (https://crrev.com/c/206927). Let's update them here, so our "defaults" are actually what we use most of the time. It might be better to avoid putting these constants here at all, but for now, it seems like we should be resilient to, for example, another test (network_WiFi_BgscanBackoff?) not resetting parameters properly. Also note that WifiProxy.configure_bgscan() is really telling *shill* what to do, which indirectly also affects wpa_supplicant bgscan parameters, but shill also schedules scanning of its own. I believe this affects tests like network_WiFi_ChannelHop, which rely on the timing of re-scan attempts after the AP goes away. Funny enough, that's pretty much why the change in https://crrev.com/c/206927 was made -- to help improve the latency for detecting rebooted APs. FIXUP: FROMLIST: ASoC: SOF: Add Sound Open Firmware driver core If CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF=y and CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_NOCODEC=m, builds fail with ld: sound/soc/sof/core.o: in function `sof_machine_check': >> sound/soc/sof/core.c:269: undefined reference to `sof_nocodec_setup' ld: sound/soc/sof/sof-acpi-dev.o: in function `sof_acpi_probe': >> sound/soc/sof/sof-acpi-dev.c:220: undefined reference to `sof_nocodec_setup' This happens because sof_nocodec_setup() is called from code built into the kernel but resides in a module. Since sof_nocodec_setup() is called unconditionally from the SOF core if CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_FORCE_NOCODEC_MODE=y, SND_SOC_SOF_NOCODEC must be built into the kernel if SND_SOC_SOF=y. Add the necessary dependency. sof_nocodec_setup() is called from sof-acpi-dev.c:sof_acpi_probe() if CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_FORCE_NOCODEC_MODE=y. This results in the second build failure if SND_SOC_SOF_NOCODEC=m and SND_SOC_SOF_ACPI=y. Since we force SND_SOC_SOF_NOCODEC=y if SND_SOC_SOF=y, and SND_SOC_SOF is selected by SND_SOC_SOF_ACPI, this problem is solved with the above change as well. This change does not affect existing Chrome OS configurations and thus does not have functional impact on shipping images.
